dimensions.assessment: Directly involves federal agencies, National Park Service units, and state/local emergency response personnel.
dimensions.evidence: consult with-- (1) State and local emergency operations officials to ensure interoperability

dimensions.assessment: Involves planning and cost estimation for emergency system upgrades, which could later improve emergency response capabilities.
dimensions.evidence: upgrade existing emergency communications centers in units of the National Park System to Next Generation 9-1-1 systems

dimensions.assessment: The source requires estimating costs for purchasing, maintaining, and operating the systems, but does not specify appropriation amounts.
dimensions.evidence: estimated costs to purchase Next Generation 9-1-1 systems for emergency communications centers

dimensions.assessment: Directs a federal agency assessment, reporting, and planning process without establishing new permanent regulatory powers over the general public.
dimensions.evidence: directs the National Park Service (NPS) to develop a plan to install Next Generation 911 (NG911) systems

dimensions.assessment: Mandates specific one-time deadlines for an assessment (1 year) and a subsequent plan (1 year after report), with ongoing implications if implemented.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall complete an assessment

missing_information: Exact dollar figures for the cost of purchasing or maintaining NG911 systems
Number of emergency communications centers currently lacking NG911 capabilities
importance_detail.rationale: This bill requires the National Park Service to conduct an assessment, report to Congress, and develop a plan to upgrade emergency communications centers to Next Generation 911 systems. While it applies across the National Park System, its immediate operational impact is preparatory and planning-focused.
